name: TRESTA NESS
survey: Tresta Ness is a settlement on a Shetland island adjacent to an oil terminal. It has a pier, a council office, an archive and a declining range of local services.
pattern: Certain unrelated things are required to be made of copper.
setting: a Shetland island community beside an oil terminal
story: Tresta Ness council is considering whether to lease the disused ferry store to the oil terminal as a training and equipment room. Signe Osla and Magnus Nicolson want the lease for its rent and the prospect of a few local jobs; Freya Manson and Catriona Bruce want the building retained for a community net-mending and workshop space. The terminal has offered £4,800 a year for five years, conditional on a decision by the end of October 1998. The shop has shortened its hours and the ferry store has stood empty since the freight service was cut. Councillor Kirsty Bain has deferred the vote while Ewan Keith checks the cost of repairs, and both camps are quietly counting votes.

pages.title: Tresta Ness Records Room
pages.content:
TRESTA NESS RECORDS ROOM

The Records Room occupies the former weigh-house behind the pier office. We hold historical ledgers, parish roll duplicates, trade receipts, and printed notices concerning Tresta Ness and the North Sound.

Hours of opening:
Tuesday: 10.00 am to 1.00 pm
Thursday: 2.00 pm to 4.30 pm
Other times by prior arrangement.

Please note the heating in the annex remains disconnected. Readers are advised to keep coats on during longer visits.

The typed holdings index covers materials deposited up to December 1996. Newer deposits are recorded in the counter ledger. Following the withdrawal of the North Sound freight run in 1995, certain pier dockets were transferred here, but administrative files remain with the council.

West Ness Chapel serves Tresta Ness and the North End. Services are held on the second and fourth Sunday of each month at 11.00 am.

pages.title: Ness Working Rooms
pages.content:
NESS WORKING ROOMS

A residents' proposal for shared work space in the former ferry store.

The ferry store beside the old pier slip has stood unheated and unused for three winters. We believe the building should remain available to people who live here for gear maintenance, net work, and bench repairs, rather than being signed over for restricted corporate use.

The council has not yet reached a decision on the future of the store. A formal alternative plan has been lodged with the clerk for consideration by members before the October deadline.

> A working use for the ferry store        nessworks.tn/proposal
> Staff        nessworks.tn/staff

pages.title: Bain Stores

BAIN STORES

Tresta Ness pier approach.

General groceries, tea, dried goods, tinned meat, matches, salt butter, and domestic coal by the sack. Paraffin supplied into your own cans. We carry the usual household lines while supplies permit.

Opening times were changed at the beginning of September 1998 due to the reduction in ferry traffic and quiet afternoons. Please read the revised hours before coming down the brae.

Newspapers arrive on the mid-morning crossing when weather allows.

pages.title: Tresta Boatmen's Association
pages.content:
TRESTA BOATMEN'S ASSOCIATION

Notices and notes for members using the east slip and pier berths. Page maintained by Bryan Napier.

Membership stands at nine inshore owners this autumn, down from fourteen in 1992. The small winch on the east slip is greased and serviceable for the winter lift-out. The water tap beside the weighbridge remains disconnected following the frost damage two years back. Please do not leave coils of leadline or spare pots on the pier deck overnight.

The freight service stopped in 1995, and gear storage has been tight since. The regular October meeting will be held in the back room at the pierhead on Tuesday 20th at 7:30pm to discuss winter arrangements for gear and creels. 

Members have enquired about the disused ferry store. The association has reached no collective view on the terminal's offer or the workshop scheme, though the secretary's personal view is that the working rooms proposal would suit those mending gear if the roof and door repairs can be funded without a levy on owners.

> Working rooms proposal        nessworks.tn/proposal
> Store decision report        tncircular.tn/store

pages.title: Inshore Baiting Rules, 1894 (scan)
pages.content:
DOCUMENT TN/REC/1894/04

RULES TO BE OBSERVED BY INSHORE CREWS AT TRESTA NESS BAITING STATION
Adopted 14th April 1894

1. No haddock or herring offal shall be cast within fifty yards of the slip.

2. Crews shall use copper bait needles when preparing the long lines at the station.

3. Lines must be coiled into the tubs before four of the clock on each working afternoon.

4. Salt bags must be returned dry to the cooperage loft.

5. Any man leaving line or hook upon the flags shall forfeit two pence to the shed keeper.

[Pencilled note at foot: 1898 season - five tubs only permitted per sixern crew - R.G.]

pages.title: Restricted: Chapel Furnishings Order, 1903
pages.content:
RESTRICTED: CHAPEL FURNISHINGS ORDER, 1903

Transcribed from Committee Minute Book 1 (1898-1914), page 28.
Kept in working files by Miriam Laurenson.

At a meeting of the West Ness Chapel Committee held 4th November 1903:

Present: Mr G. Isbister, Mr T. Laurenson, Mr D. Gray, Miss M. Sinclair.

Item 3: Furnishings.
The committee orders a copper collection plate for the chapel.
Resolved that eighteen deal benches be fitted with iron brackets along the north aisle.
Resolved that four brass wall-sconces be procured from Messrs. J. Smith & Son, Leith, at a cost not exceeding fifteen shillings each, carriage included.
Resolved that the floor of the vestry be laid with linoleum of plain pattern, the joiner to supply felt underlay.

Copied by M. Laurenson, Caretaker, for the inventory records, 1981.

pages.title: Ness Lines - chapel computer
pages.content:
Thread: chapel computer
[bertie] A reminder for those using the machine at West Ness Chapel when doing parish notes or inventory lists. Please log off when you are done.
[tam_g] Is there a general password for the vestry machine or do we need our own account from the council clerk?
[bertie] The chapel's starting logins used each person's surname followed by the year they started, all lower case and with no spaces. It saved time then, though I wish people would change them.
[miriam] I am still using the one I was given when the chapel computer was set up. I have not changed it.
[tam_g] Right, thank you Miriam. I only needed to check an order date from last winter.

pages.title: Ness Lines - office computers
pages.content:
Thread: office computers
[bertie] I was up at the terminal training office on Monday looking at the monitor in room two. A few machines are still sitting on default settings.
[innes_p] Most of us don't touch the training terminals unless a safety refresher is scheduled from Aberdeen.
[bertie] When I set up the training office logins, every new staff account there was issued the same starting password, verbena. They really ought to change them.
[magnus] I still have the one I was given when the account was set up. I will get round to changing it when the course is finished.
[bertie] It takes two minutes Magnus. Just run the account utility from the prompt.

pages.title: Ness Lines - the ferry store figures
pages.content:
Thread: the ferry store figures
[freya] Could someone from the council please confirm the exact repair estimate for the ferry store? We have £1,200 pledged privately towards materials for the community rooms, but we cannot assess what remains to be found without the full figures.
[ewan] The builder from Brae gave a preliminary roof estimate of £2,300 last Tuesday. The wiring figure has not arrived yet from Lerwick. Until both are in hand, the council cannot state the total cost of repair.
[kirsty] Both proposals will be discussed if the estimate is ready before the October meeting. Neither decision has been taken and procedure will be followed.
[tam_g] The roof has leaked into the north corner since the freight service ended. It won't get cheaper by waiting.

pages.title: Ness Lines - training room use
pages.content:
Thread: training room use
[magnus] To clarify regarding the terminal's lease proposal for the ferry store: the plan is for equipment instruction, safety briefings, and pipe-handling modules. There is also the possibility of two part-time posts for storekeeping and site maintenance, though these are explicitly not approved by head office yet.
[bryan] Will those posts be local people or contractors brought across on the ferry? And will they be permanent, or just for the five-year lease period?
[magnus] I cannot give guarantees on staffing that head office has not signed off on. I only state what the proposed budget permits.
[signe] Even without the posts confirmed, the rent of £4,800 a year is guaranteed income for the council when funds are short everywhere else.
[bertie] Let us keep the discussion to the published details please.

pages.title: Ness Lines - shop opening hours
pages.content:
Thread: shop opening hours
[sheila] Notice to customers: Bain's Stores is now operating winter hours of 9 am to 1 pm, Monday to Saturday. The afternoon trade was simply too low through September to justify running the heaters. Saturday paraffin orders must be placed by Thursday noon.
[tam_g] It makes it difficult for folks working out at the terminal gate to pick up groceries before evening.
[bertie] Sheila, if an existing order was placed on Wednesday, can it still be collected Saturday morning before 1 pm?
[sheila] Yes Bertie, anything ordered before Thursday noon will be boxed and ready on Saturday morning as usual.

pages.title: Ness Lines - net mending tables
pages.content:
Thread: net mending tables
[catriona] For the community workshop proposal, the plan requires space for two net-mending tables and a shared repair bench for domestic joinery and gear upkeep. If the ferry store is granted, we have the timber promised.
[miriam] I can offer to help with cleaning the floor if it goes ahead, but the chapel cannot lend its weekday room in the afternoon. There are too few volunteers to supervise the building outside service hours.
[bryan] If the group is allowed to use the store, I am willing to bring my hand-cart down and help clear the scrap iron and old pallets.
[freya] Thank you Bryan. We will keep a note of all offers of practical help until the council reaches a decision.

pages.title: Ness Lines - circular deliveries
pages.content:
Thread: circular deliveries
[malcolm] We need a volunteer to deliver twelve October Circular copies on the north side. The previous deliverer stopped due to poor health, and I cannot manage the north lane on foot this month.
[sheila] If someone takes the run, Malcolm, you can leave the bundle for collection at the shop before 1 pm.
[bertie] I have to drive up to the north end on Thursday afternoon to look at a modem for Mrs Halcrow. I can take the twelve copies if they are left at the shop.
[malcolm] Thank you Bertie. I will leave them with Sheila on Wednesday morning.

pages.title: Council defers ferry store decision
pages.content:
COUNCIL DEFERS FERRY STORE DECISION

At the September meeting, Councillor Kirsty Bain deferred the vote on the disused ferry store until Ewan Keith receives the outstanding repair figures. The slater's estimate for the south pitch of the roof is £2,300, but the wiring assessment has not arrived from Lerwick.

The terminal company has offered £4,800 per annum on a five-year lease for use as a training room, conditional on an agreement by 31 October. Magnus Nicolson stated that two part-time local posts may follow if the lease goes through, though these are not yet formally approved by the terminal board.

Freya Manson spoke for the workshop group, reporting that six prospective users have come forward and £1,200 has been pledged towards repairs to keep the space for net-mending and gear storage.

Both sides spoke at length. The matter will return to the table when the wiring figures are tabled.

FROM THE COUNCIL PAPERS

We have had two inquiries regarding access to the older papers kept in the council office safe. Ewan Keith reminds residents that while the office is only staffed part-time, public access is maintained under the usual procedure.

The council office holds the 1851 Weights Inspection Order, an early instruction to the local weights inspector. Anyone may obtain a copy by filing form R-3 with the council office and naming the order. Ewan Keith handles requests and sends the copy by email. The office keeps the original with its other early council papers.

pages.title: Next council meeting
pages.content:
NEXT COUNCIL MEETING

The next ordinary meeting of Tresta Ness Council will take place on Monday 26 October 1998 at 6.30 pm in the council room.

Business will include ordinary pier accounts, coal allowance vouchers, and the deferred matter of the former freight store.

The lease offer from the oil terminal and the alternative proposal for working rooms will both be placed on the agenda, provided the wiring estimate is ready in time. Mr Keith has obtained a builder's estimate of £2,300 for the east roof pitch and gutters, but the electrical figure is still outstanding. No vote has yet been taken.

Members of the public may attend. Space is limited to twelve seats.

Kirsty Bain, Chair.

pages.title: Training room proposal
pages.content:
TRAINING ROOM PROPOSAL

Statement from Magnus Nicolson, Training Supervisor.
Date: 2 October 1998.

The terminal training office has formally placed an offer before Tresta Ness Council to lease the disused ferry store building adjacent to the pier.

The terminal offers £4,800 per annum on a five-year agreement. This offer is conditional upon a council decision being reached before the end of October 1998, to allow repair work to be scheduled prior to winter.

The store has stood vacant since the freight service ended in 1995. If leased, the ground floor would be converted into an equipment instruction area for handling gear and containment kit. Subject to budget clearance, two part-time local posts for store maintenance may be created, though these are not yet formally approved.

This office is aware of competing views regarding the building. Queries should be directed to Ellen Gilbert.

> Council report        tncircular.tn/store
> Alternative proposal        nessworks.tn/proposal

pages.title: Chapel caretaking
pages.content:
CHAPEL CARETAKING

Notes on the upkeep of West Ness Chapel, compiled by Miriam Laurenson.

Miriam Laurenson started as chapel caretaker in 1972.

The roof over the north aisle was renewed in 1984, but the damp in the weekday room requires coal fires to be kept up through the winter months. The weekday room now closes in the afternoons because there are too few volunteers to tend the grate and sit with visitors.

Several people have asked whether the weekday room could be used during the week for net-mending and gear drying. I have had to say no, as we have no spare floor space and the chapel cannot have damp gear piled against the pews. I support retaining the ferry store for work space because the chapel has no spare room for the net-menders.

> Working rooms proposal        nessworks.tn/proposal

pages.title: A working use for the ferry store
pages.content:
A WORKING USE FOR THE FERRY STORE

The freight service ended in 1995 and the store has been empty since. Our proposal is to reopen the stone building as a dry, shared working room for islanders.

We currently have six potential regular users and £1,200 in initial pledges toward immediate roof patching and lighting. The floor plan provides space for two net-mending tables and a shared bench for small repairs, with room left for seasonal gear storage.

We cannot complete a full budget until Ewan Keith completes the full repair estimate, including the outstanding wiring figure. Freya Manson notes that granting a five-year lease to the oil terminal would prevent the store being used as a local workshop for that period. Catriona Bruce has asked that both proposals be heard together at the same meeting so councillors may compare community use against commercial hire.

This proposal remains pending council review.

pages.title: Shop hours and orders
pages.content:
SHOP HOURS AND ORDERS

Notice from Sheila Niven:

From Monday 7th September 1998, Bain Stores opens Monday to Saturday, 9:00 am to 1:00 pm only. We are closed all day Sunday.

Afternoon trade has not covered the cost of staffing or counter heating since the freight run was taken off. We are sorry for any inconvenience to households on the far side of the Ness.

Paraffin must be ordered by 12 noon on Thursday for collection on Saturday morning. Please bring sound drums with working stoppers.

Replacement copper terminals for the counter brass weights scale have been ordered from Aberdeen and should be fitted before winter.

Regarding the ferry store on the pier: either proposal would be welcome if it brings trade back past the door during the week, but Bain Stores takes no view on council business.

> Ferry store report        tncircular.tn/store

records.title: Tresta Ness Weights Inspection Order, 1851
records.content:
TRESTA NESS WEIGHTS INSPECTION ORDER, 1851

At Tresta Ness, the fourth day of August, one thousand eight hundred and fifty-one.

It is ordered that the burgh inspector shall attend upon the pier twice yearly, upon the first lawful day of March and of September, to examine all steelyards, beam-scales, tubs and cran-measures used in the trade of fish, salt, or general freight within the boundaries of the haven.

The inspector shall mark each checked measure with the copper inspection seal.

Any barrel, basket, or balance found wanting or uncertified shall be withheld from the landing stage until adjusted and newly marked. The fee for each examination shall be fourpence, payable by the owner of the gear.

Certified a true copy from the Tresta Ness burgh minute book.
Ewan Keith, Records Officer, Tresta Ness Council.

insider.title: North Grazing Lease, 1886
insider.content:
NORTH GRAZING LEASE, 1886

Extract from Estate Register (Volume 14, Ness Enclosures), held on file for site boundary verification.

Memorandum of Agreement between Thomas Henderson of Gremista and James Isbister, tenant in Tresta Ness.

The tenant James Isbister enters into possession of the fourteen acres known as the North Grazing for a term of six years from Martinmas 1886, at an annual rent of nine pounds sterling.

The tenant shall fit copper gate hinges to the north grazing enclosure.

All stone dykes must be kept sheep-proof by the tenant without claim for timber or lime against the proprietor. The peats are to be cut only upon the low bank towards the wick, and no turf shall be pared from the headland pasture.

Copied for the Terminal Works Safety Archive, April 1978.

directives.task: Read at least three pages in the Reality Viewer.
directives.subject: Directive 14-1: orientation
directives.body:
Agent,

Before sending any traffic, read the material Desk 9 recovered in the Reality Viewer: Tresta Ness Records Room, Ness Lines, Tresta Ness Circular, Tresta Ness Council, Tresta Terminal Training Office, West Ness Chapel, Ness Working Rooms, Bain Stores and Tresta Boatmen's Association. Reading is passive and does not pass through the connection, so the local intelligence cannot detect it.

Use this stage to note the staff names, the arguments on the forum, and which offices hold which records. You will need those details later, and any message you send to ask for them will be logged on the connection.

This directive closes when you have read at least three pages.

D. Okonkwo-Vance

siteNames: Tresta Ness Records Room, Ness Lines, Tresta Ness Circular, Tresta Ness Council, Tresta Terminal Training Office, West Ness Chapel, Ness Working Rooms, Bain Stores and Tresta Boatmen's Association

directives.task: Find a seed fragment and save it to Files. Start with Tresta Ness Records Room.
directives.subject: Directive 14-2: first fragment
directives.body:
Agent,

Desk 9's initial survey noted a scanned fishing station rule sheet on Tresta Ness Records Room. In a reality of this age, the seed usually appears first in the oldest records the town holds. Look for a detail that is given more weight in the text than seems warranted.

When you locate the document, use the Save page function in the viewer. Saving writes a static copy to your local files which cannot be altered from the other side. Unsaved pages in the viewer remain on their system and can be changed at any time.

This directive closes when one of your saved documents holds a fragment.

D. Okonkwo-Vance

make.docKind: a scanned fishing station rule sheet

directives.task: Transmit the saved fragment from the HQ Console.
directives.subject: Directive 14-3: transmission
directives.body:
Agent,

Open the HQ Console, select the saved document, and transmit it. If the document contains a valid fragment, the console will report RESONANCE.

Do not transmit saved pages at random to test them. Every transmission passes outbound through the connection and increases the likelihood that the local intelligence will register our presence.

This directive closes when the console reports resonance.

D. Okonkwo-Vance

directives.task: Get Ellen Gilbert to send you North Grazing Lease, 1886. They only send it to Tresta Terminal Training Office staff.
directives.subject: Directive 14-4: internal circulation
directives.body:
Agent,

Ellen Gilbert at Tresta Terminal Training Office holds an unpublished document (a typed copy of an old grazing lease) which Desk 9 believes contains a fragment. It is only sent out by internal email when requested by another member of Tresta Terminal Training Office staff.

To obtain it, you will need to log in as a colleague. The staff portal at Tresta Terminal Training Office gives access to that person's email account, and a request sent from an internal address will be treated as routine. Small institutions often give every new account the same starting password, and not everyone changes theirs. Someone will usually have complained about it in a public post.

Keep your message brief, and do not use the account for anything else. Staff members usually notice if their account shows unfamiliar activity.

This directive closes when you transmit a fragment from the document.

D. Okonkwo-Vance

make.docKind: a typed copy of an old grazing lease

directives.task: Get into West Ness Chapel's restricted file (Chapel Furnishings Order, 1903) and transmit its fragment.
directives.subject: Directive 14-5: restricted holdings
directives.body:
Agent,

West Ness Chapel holds a restricted document (a transcribed chapel furnishings order) which Desk 9 could index but not open. Accessing it requires a staff username and password.

The login page gives the format used for staff usernames. For the password, check the public pages first. Starting passwords there were built to a fixed scheme from personal details. Someone on the forum has explained the scheme, and the details it uses are usually on public pages.

Note that login submissions pass through the connection whether they succeed or fail. Confirm the credentials before you enter them so that you do not make repeated attempts.

This directive closes when you transmit a fragment from the restricted file.

D. Okonkwo-Vance

directives.task: Find out which record to request, file form R-3 with Tresta Ness Council, and transmit the fragment from the reply.
directives.subject: Directive 14-6: records request
directives.body:
Agent,

Older records at Tresta Ness Council are not held online, but copies are released on submission of form R-3. Desk 9 does not have the reference for the specific record required. Check Tresta Ness Circular first, or contact a local resident who works with the holdings and give a plausible reason for the enquiry.

You will also need to state a reason for the request on form R-3 itself. Requests without one are less likely to be granted.

The office sends the requested record by email through the connection. If the reply is delayed, fails to arrive, or contains unexpected text, take that as an indication that the local intelligence is interfering with traffic.

This directive closes when you transmit a fragment from the reply.

D. Okonkwo-Vance

advisory.task: Flood at least one document in the Scanner.
advisory.subject: Advisory: the connection has been registered
advisory.body:
Agent,

Monitoring reports that the local intelligence has registered the connection.

From this point on, any data reaching your terminal, including incoming mail and viewer pages you have not saved,may have been modified in transit. Before relying on any document, load it into the Scanner and flood it. Altered sections will visibly shake under the flood. Be aware that repeated floods degrade the sample and make the reading less reliable.

This advisory closes when you have used the Scanner once.

Monitoring

inject.task: Inject the reverse seed from the HQ Console.
inject.subject: Directive 14-7: injection
inject.body:
Agent,

Desk 9 confirms that your accumulated resonance is sufficient for injection. The HQ Console is now offering injection.

Proceed with the reverse seed injection immediately. Waiting provides no operational advantage, and the local intelligence will continue to trace the connection whether or not you send further traffic.

This directive closes on injection.

D. Okonkwo-Vance

hqMail.subject: Assignment 0x4279 (TRESTA NESS): field brief
hqMail.body:
Agent,

You have been assigned Reality 0x4279, local name TRESTA NESS. Tresta Ness is a settlement on a Shetland island adjacent to an oil terminal. It has a pier, a council office, an archive and a declining range of local services. Desk 9 estimates it at three to five weeks old. The inhabitants (non-canonical) will report a longer history, as their memories have been generated to remain consistent with the local state.

Standard reconciliation procedure applies:

1. Locate fragments of the reality's seed. These appear as ordinary facts, distinguished by the property that nothing in the reality is able to change them.
2. Save each fragment to Files and transmit it from the HQ console. The console will report RESONANCE if the fragment is genuine.
3. When resonance is sufficient, the console will offer injection. Inject the reverse seed to complete reconciliation.

Your cover identity is S. Dunmore (dunmore.s@nessnet.tn). Outgoing traffic on the connection uses this name unless otherwise configured. Reading material on the connection is passive and remains private.

The local intelligence (designation pending) has not yet detected the connection. Once it does, incoming records may be altered in transit. Your poison allocation is loaded in the Scanner. Use it sparingly, as the instability rebounds after each flood.

Form 77-R will be filed automatically at the close of the assignment. If you have not viewed the orientation film, a copy has been placed on your desktop by Training.

D. Okonkwo-Vance
Desk 14, Canonical Restoration

hqMail.subject: Reality poison: your allocation and the rebound
hqMail.body:
This notice is issued to all field agents at the start of an assignment.

The Scanner floods a reality's lesser processes for several seconds. During the flood, records altered by the local intelligence cannot hold their state and will visibly shake on screen. Statements that are false only because a resident believed or misreported them are part of the local state and will not shake. The Scanner does not detect false statements, only alteration.

Up to three documents may be held in the Scanner at a time.

Please note that the instability rebounds after use. A second flood shortly after the first draws increased attention from the local process and produces a less clear reading. Subsequent floods degrade the reading further.

Allocations

updates.text: The early closing is hard on the pensioners along the pier too, Sheila. We used to rely on the four o'clock post van to drop the paraffin tins by the slip.
Bottled gas deliveries will run on Tuesday mornings only through October. Please ensure empty cylinders are set outside the gate before eight.
Ewan, the 1984 survey noted salt rot in the collar beams as well as the north slates. The terminal offer would lift the whole cost off the rates.
Search facility temporarily slow while the drive index settles. Some archive entries from 1991 appeared with altered file dates this morning without explanation.
We have had two more offers of surplus timber from the yard at Hillswick. The space would not stand idle for a single month.
The public gallery for the October planning discussion will be restricted to twenty chairs due to dry rot behind the lower wall panels.
The hall monitor was humming when I walked through at six. The screen had the cursor blinking at the top corner, though nobody had been booked in since dinner.
The rent is only good if there is still a village here to spend it. If the gear menders have to pack their tubs to Lerwick, we lose more than two storekeeping jobs.
The vestry telephone rang once at quarter past seven and stopped. The notebook on the desk had been shifted an inch towards the window, but the bolt was drawn.
The wind is getting up from the south-east tonight. I have left the bundle wrapped in heavy polythene on Sheila's back step so it will keep dry.
Clerk Keith confirms the electrician's report on the ferry store wiring will be tabled on Monday noon, ahead of the final agenda printing.
